correctness.rationale: The prime-field numerator recurrence and source Proposition 4.1(a) connect precisely the required nonsquare events to roots of \(z^2+1\) and \(z^4+3z^2+1\). Root counts are proved for \(p=2\), \(p=5\), inert odd primes, and \(p\equiv1,9\pmod{20}\). Coprimality and a homogeneous two-step polynomial rule establish absence of ALL later events whenever the quartic has no root, not just tested indices. CRT yields exact finite-period joint probabilities; excluded primes yield an explicit positive-integer index-3 counterexample. The independent standard-library verifier exercises modular counts and rational arithmetic, with finite tests not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The primary source explicitly requests density of starts with a specified number of failures. An exact joint law at the two earliest possible failure indices for every multiplier, followed by a sharp and complete Bernoulli all-time law on an infinite naturally defined prime-splitting family, supplies a quantitative solution rather than a routine point check. The result distinguishes a genuine threshold in the preimage tree: when the depth-two fiber is empty every deeper fiber is empty.
